components.label: A person approves or edits first

plan-hitl.omitted: Pages checked: Ask Devin, Linear, Jira, Using Playbooks, gallery bulk-plan-backlog and prd-to-tickets (docs.devin.ai). They describe a person working with Devin in conversation or Devin posting plan comments with open questions, but none states whether a person must approve or edit the plan before work starts.

plan-persist.name: PRD to tickets
plan-persist.summary: In the gallery example Devin reads a PRD and creates Linear tickets, so the plan lives in the tracker. The bulk-plan example instead posts the plan as a comment on each ticket. Ask Devin produces a prompt that starts a session; the page does not say it is saved.
plan-persist.short: Yes: Linear tickets and ticket comments

plan-contents.name: PRD to tickets
plan-contents.summary: The page's example output is tickets with an ID, title, T-shirt size, dependencies on other tickets, description, acceptance criteria and likely file paths; it is an example, not a guaranteed format. The Ask Devin page does not say its breakdown carries criteria or dependencies.
plan-contents.short: Mixed: example tickets carry both; Ask Devin unstated

verify.name: unknown
verify.summary: Devin runs existing tests, lint and type checks in its own environment and iterates until tests pass before submitting a PR. Which checks run is set by the prompt, playbook or repo skill, not by a fixed pipeline.
verify.short: Tests, lint, type checks named in prompt

loop-across.name: Automations
loop-across.summary: An automation fires on a trigger (schedule, ticket, GitHub, Slack or webhook) and starts a session with a saved prompt. A finished session choosing the next ticket by itself is not documented.
loop-across.short: Triggers start sessions; next-ticket pick undocumented

loop-drive.name: Automations
loop-drive.summary: The page says events start sessions automatically, without a person tagging Devin, once a person has created the automation.

demoable.summary: The Free self-serve plan lists limited Devin usage, plus access to Devin Review and DeepWiki.

plan-hitl.name: Specification Mode
plan-hitl.summary: Droid researches read-only and proposes a plan; nothing is edited until the person approves, and the person can approve or keep iterating on it. In Missions, execution starts once the plan is approved.

plan-persist.name: Specification Mode
plan-persist.summary: Once approved, the plan can optionally be saved as a dated Markdown file (default .factory/docs). Whether Spec Mode splits it into separate tasks is not documented.
plan-persist.short: Yes: Spec Mode can save a file

plan-contents.name: Missions plan
plan-contents.summary: A Mission plan is features grouped into milestones, and each feature has its own validation criteria visible in the Factory App. Explicit dependency edges between features are not documented (ordering is mentioned).
plan-contents.short: Mixed: Missions criteria; dependencies not documented

verify.name: Validation workers
verify.summary: Validation workers run at the end of each milestone, verifying its work, and Missions validate their own work by exercising the running application.
verify.short: Validation workers at each milestone end

loop-across.name: Mission orchestrator
loop-across.summary: After each feature or milestone finishes, the orchestrator reviews progress and starts the next work from the plan.
loop-across.short: Orchestrator starts next feature after each

loop-drive.name: Mission orchestrator
loop-drive.summary: After approval an orchestrator manages execution; the person can pause it and talk to it to recover.

plan-hitl.name: Research, plan and iterate
plan-hitl.summary: The cloud agent shows a plan before making changes; the person reviews it and iterates with follow-up prompts until it matches their intent, then asks it to implement. In Copilot CLI plan mode the person chooses to accept the plan before autopilot starts.
plan-hitl.short: Yes: review and iterate on the plan

plan-persist.omitted: Pages checked (docs.github.com): Research, plan and iterate; Copilot CLI autopilot; Copilot on GitHub.com; Best practices; Dynamic workflows. They say the plan is shown in the conversation or executed by the same session; none says it is saved as a file or tracker items.

plan-contents.omitted: Pages checked (docs.github.com): Research, plan and iterate; Copilot CLI autopilot; Best practices; improve-a-project tutorial. None says a plan is split into tasks carrying acceptance criteria or dependencies (the tutorial has the person check criteria on issues Copilot creates from findings, which is not plan output).

verify.name: Cloud agent session
verify.summary: The agent works in its own GitHub Actions environment, where it runs tests and linters to validate changes. How the results decide whether it keeps going before opening the PR is not documented.
verify.short: Runs tests and linters; gate not documented

loop-across.name: Agentic Workflows work queue (gh-aw)
loop-across.summary: On the gh-aw site (GitHub Next), a native work queue holds work as a dependency graph; the scheduler picks eligible work and a task waits for its predecessors' results. Copilot automations are documented only as trigger-started runs, not as picking the next ready issue.
loop-across.short: gh-aw work queue; Copilot automations: not documented

loop-drive.name: Agentic Workflows work queue (gh-aw)
loop-drive.summary: Automated once the producer, dispatcher and worker workflows are published on the default branch.

plan-hitl.name: Software Factory triage
plan-hitl.summary: The triage agent runs as an automation that checks every 5 minutes: it prioritizes issues, checks dependencies, establishes acceptance criteria, then applies the ready-for-dev label. The page describes no step where a person approves or edits the result; the person writes the issues and acceptance criteria beforehand.

plan-persist.name: ready-for-dev label
plan-persist.summary: The output of triage is the GitHub issue carrying the ready-for-dev label, which the developer automation watches. A separate task list or plan file is not documented.

plan-contents.name: Software Factory triage
plan-contents.summary: The triage agent checks the issue's dependencies and establishes acceptance criteria before applying ready-for-dev. How the criteria are written is not documented.
plan-contents.short: Yes: triage checks dependencies and criteria

verify.name: Goal Completion Loop
verify.summary: In the SDK, a second judge LLM audits the transcript for evidence, such as test output, that proves the objective is complete. The Issue to PR automation lists running tests as a step but does not document what happens when they fail.
verify.short: SDK: judge LLM audits transcript for proof

loop-across.name: Software Factory
loop-across.summary: Four automations poll every 5 minutes. GitHub labels and statuses are the queue, and the next labeled issue is taken at the next poll.

loop-drive.name: Software Factory
loop-drive.summary: Automated after a person turns on the four automations and files the issues.
loop-drive.short: Automated once a person sets it up

demoable.summary: The GitHub repository states an MIT license and says agents can be run locally, in Docker, on VMs, or anywhere an agent server backend runs.

plan-hitl.name: Plan Mode
plan-hitl.summary: The agent writes a plan that the person reviews and edits in chat or as markdown, then clicks Build when satisfied. If it is not right, the docs advise reverting and refining the plan rather than patching a bad build with follow-ups.
plan-hitl.short: Yes: edit the plan, then Build

plan-persist.name: Plan Mode
plan-persist.summary: The plan opens as an editable virtual file saved by default in the person's home directory; Save to workspace moves it into the repo for sharing.
plan-persist.short: Yes: plan file; Save to workspace

plan-contents.omitted: Pages checked (cursor.com): Plan Mode docs and help, Agent overview, Prompting agents, Agentic coding help, Multi-agent help, Projects. None says plan steps carry acceptance criteria. Multi-agent help says Build in Parallel keeps dependent steps in order but not how dependencies are written.

verify.name: Cloud Agents
verify.summary: The cloud agent can build, test and interact with the changed software, and can control a desktop and browser. The docs say an agent that cannot run tests cannot close the loop. A fixed pre-delivery gate that always runs is not documented.
verify.short: Agent builds and tests itself; no fixed gate

loop-across.name: Automations
loop-across.summary: A trigger (schedule, source-control, Slack, webhook, Linear event) starts a cloud agent with a saved prompt. One run starting the next is not documented as chaining.
loop-across.short: Triggers start runs; chaining not documented

loop-drive.name: Automations
loop-drive.summary: Automated after a person creates and activates the automation.

demoable.summary: The docs say Cloud Agents require a paid Cursor plan and are charged at API pricing for the selected model.

plan-hitl.name: Plan mode
plan-hitl.summary: Claude writes a plan and does not edit source files until it is approved. The person can open the plan in a text editor (Ctrl+G) and edit it; approving offers three choices: continue in auto mode, continue approving each edit, or keep planning.
plan-hitl.short: Yes: edit it, approve, or keep planning

plan-persist.name: Agent teams
plan-persist.summary: In an agent team the lead creates tasks in a shared task list, stored locally under ~/.claude/tasks/{team-name}/. Agent teams are experimental and off by default.
plan-persist.short: Yes: agent teams task list on disk

plan-contents.name: Agent teams
plan-contents.summary: Tasks in the shared task list can depend on other tasks: a pending task with unresolved dependencies cannot be claimed until they are completed. Acceptance criteria on a task are not documented.
plan-contents.short: Mixed: agent teams have dependencies; criteria undocumented

verify.name: /goal
verify.summary: After every turn a separate small model checks the condition; if it is not met, Claude starts another turn. The evaluator runs no commands and reads no files, so the condition must be something the transcript shows, such as a test result.

loop-across.name: Agent teams
loop-across.summary: In an agent team, a teammate that finishes a task picks up the next unassigned, unblocked task from the shared list on its own. Experimental and off by default.

loop-drive.name: Agent teams
loop-drive.summary: Automated after a person starts the team.
loop-drive.short: Automated once a person starts the team

destination.summary: The overview points to parallel subagents, background agents, scheduled Routines and the Agent SDK for custom orchestration.

queue.name: Issues, Projects, Cycles
queue.summary: Issues are Linear's fundamental unit of work; Projects group issues around a shared outcome, and Cycles are a team's repeating planning period.

queue.name: Work items (formerly issues)
queue.summary: Work items are the building blocks of Jira and can represent a story, bug, task or another work type.

queue.name: Issues, sub-issues, Projects
queue.summary: Issues track bugs, features and ideas; sub-issues add hierarchies between issues, and Projects is integrated with issues to plan and track a team's work.
